text:
alex: Hey team :wave: Trying to get the Next.js SSR starter working with the LlamaIndex example and hitting a weird auth+retry issue when rendering server-side. Client requests are fine, SSR sometimes returns 401s.

mira: ugh, that sounds annoying. Are you using the Node SDK or the edge runtime? Any minimal repro? :thinking_face:

alex: Node runtime (not edge). Using @redwood/sdk v0.12.1 in a Next.js app (app-dir, server components do fetch). Env set as REDWOOD_API_KEY. Intermittent 401 on the very first SSR request after a cold start, then subsequent requests succeed.

sanjay: Could be related to our retry wrapper not handling server-only envs correctly. Do you see any retry logs in server console?

alex: yep here's the server console snippet:

```
Error: 401 Unauthorized
    at RedwoodClient.request (/workspace/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/lib/index.js:482:23)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
    at async renderToHTML (/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/server/render.js:1234:20)
Retrying request (1/2)
```

mira: The log looks like the SDK is retrying, but 401 shouldn't be retried unless it's transient. What kind of cred are you using? Long-lived API key or short-lived token via KMS? :bulb:

alex: long-lived key hard-coded for repro (development only). I also tried copying the exact same fetch from client-side and it succeeds.

olivia: Are you using the same package as the Python LlamaIndex example? There are two SDK packages and dev experience parity is still messy.

alex: The LlamaIndex example uses the python client. I'm trying to call the Redwood hosted API from Node SSR to run index queries during SSR for SEO. The python side behaves as expected.

sanjay: Quick theory: Next's server runtime may reuse some connection pooling that interacts with our retry/backoff on 401; the SDK had a bug where a non-idempotent auth header mutation happened on retry, causing the second attempt to succeed but first to fail. I'll check the token handling logic.

mira: Workaround for now: don't let SSR hit the API on first paint — render a shell and call server action or edge function after hydration. Or extract the API call into server-only API route that sets header freshly.

alex: Tried moving to an API route, still saw a 401 once in awhile, but much less frequent.

olivia: Can you try pinning @redwood/sdk to 0.12.0? We changed a small retry behavior in 0.12.1 that affected SSR. If that makes it go away, it's probably the regression.

alex: Pinning to 0.12.0 made it stop throwing 401s in my repro. Good catch.

sanjay: Ok that's the regression then. I'll open a hotfix PR to revert the retry logic for server runtimes. Thanks for the repro. Can you attach the minimal app to the issue? makes it faster to validate.

alex: Will do — I'll push a tiny repro to devex/examples/next-llama-ssr and link it here. Also filing issue #734 with steps.

mira: For docs: we should add a note about SSR and recommended env var names (REDWOOD_SERVER_KEY vs NEXT_PUBLIC_...). That has tripped people up before. Also mention pinning versions until the fix lands.

dev-bot: CI: build passed for branch alex/next-llama-repro (commit bd12f3) :white_check_mark:

alex: Confirmed the repro is in the repo and linked in the issue. Thanks all, workaround + pin helped. I'll follow up once the PR lands so we can upgrade.

sanjay: I'll target a patch release this week to 0.12.2 and link the changelog. Sorry for the friction — appreciate the quick triage.

mira: Nice bug hunt :magnifying_glass: Can we add a tiny integration test in devex/examples to catch SSR auth regressions? Should be quick.

alex: Good idea. I'll add a test that hits the API route with a fake key and asserts no retry mutation.

olivia: Thanks for the detailed logs + repro, alex. This helps a lot for SDK parity between Node and python flows. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks everyone! Filing follow-up PRs shortly.
